title: D-01: Stored plate-reader fluorescence signals
question: What numerical and spatial patterns are present in the supplied native results?
materials: Three original VMR result files, one VWP protocol and source-specific cadmium experiment notes.
methods: Decompress JSON and map values with the stored physical row/column indices. Summarize each GUID/gain separately.
Plot independent native-value colour scales. No gain conversion, condition assignment, blank or OD correction.
results: Recovered 150 readings across 3 distinct stored results, with 50 physical wells A1:E10 each.
gain 2939: range 23036-260000, 29/50 entries equal 260000; gain 2976: range 27641-260000, 13/50 entries equal 260000; gain 933: range 22-3328, 0/50 entries equal 260000.
conclusion: The three stored result sets contain 150 readings across wells A1-E10. Native signals vary across wells and gain settings. The exported readings and coordinates provide a reproducible numerical record of the plate measurements.

figures.caption: Stored fluorescence by physical well. Each result uses its own colour scale; gains differ. No condition labels or uncertainty estimates are assigned.

references: Original VMR ProtocolResult fields and cadmium_experiment_notes.md: R-WET-12AUG-VOYAGER / R-WET-12AUG-LAYOUT.
scope_and_assumptions: Each VMR GUID and gain defines a separate stored result set. Explicit file coordinates define the wells, and values retain their native scale. The archive has no accepted well-to-clone/dose/control map or gain/flag calibration; source records also differ in instrument naming. This analysis reports native signals without blank, biomass or dose-response correction.
